title: Reality preservation and trace descent across constant extensions
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $m\ge1$, set $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and write $g:X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m\to X_0$. Let $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ be a constructible Weil sheaf of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and denote by $\mathcal F^{(m)}=(M,\theta^{[m]})$ its restriction as a $k_m$-Weil sheaf, with the iterated Weil map of [lem-zl-constant-extension-weil-heart-equivalence].

If $\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-real [def-wf-iota-real], then $\mathcal F^{(m)}$ is $\iota$-real. For every real $w$, if $\mathcal F^{(m)}$ has a finite mixed filtration of weights at most $w$, then $g_*g^*\mathcal F$, formed with the inverse image of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] with their induced Weil structures and interpreted in the $k_0$-constructible Weil heart, has a finite mixed filtration of weights at most $w$. Here $g^*\mathcal F$ corresponds to $\mathcal F^{(m)}$ under the exact equivalence between the $k_0$-Weil heart on the $m$ cyclic geometric sheets and the $k_m$-Weil heart on one sheet; its subobjects, quotient Frobenius operators and purity weights are the corresponding ones.

There is a morphism $\operatorname{Tr}:g_*g^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ in the constructible Weil heart whose geometric-stalk map is summation over the $m$ sheets and whose composite with the diagonal unit $\eta:\mathcal F\to g_*g^*\mathcal F$ of the adjunction between this inverse and direct image is $m\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal F}$. Thus $m^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}$ is a Weil-equivariant retraction of $\eta$. In particular, mixedness of $\mathcal F^{(m)}$ of weights at most $w$ implies mixedness of $\mathcal F$ of weights at most $w$. No lissity, geometric connectedness or semisimplicity is assumed.

proof.text: At a closed point $z$ above $x$, the heart equivalence gives $F_z\sim F_x^f$, $f=m/\gcd(\deg x,m)\ge1$. Apply the power-spectrum lemma to $F_x$ over $\Qlb$. Conjugation stability, with multiplicities, is preserved, so the definition of reality gives reality of $\mathcal F^{(m)}$.

Transport the given filtration through the inverse cyclic-sheet heart equivalence. It ends in $N=g^*\mathcal F$ in the $k_0$-heart; inclusions, quotients, local operators and absolute residue sizes correspond, so its pure quotient weights remain $u_i\le w$.

Over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X_0$, $g$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k_0}k_m)$; a $k_0$-basis of $k_m$ generates this finite $A$-module. Thus $g$ is finite, as is its geometric base change. Hence $X_{0,m}$ is separated of finite type over $k_0$, as finite-pushforward punctual purity requires. The finite-adic direct image is exact on hearts, with its canonical Weil lift. Push the Step-2 filtration forward: its quotients are $g_*(N_i/N_{i-1})$, pure of weights $u_i$ by finite-pushforward punctual purity. This is the required mixed filtration on $P=g_*g^*\mathcal F$.

The constant-extension equivalence supplies the $m$ clopen sheets; in the projection coordinates $a\otimes b\mapsto a\sigma(b)$ each maps identically to $X$. Apply the split-sheet adjunction to identify $P$ underneath with $\bigoplus_\sigma M$, its unit with the diagonal, and $T$ with the global summation map, including on geometric stalks.

By the sheet Weil-action lemma, $\theta_P$ permutes components and applies $\theta$. Hence $T\theta_P((v_\sigma))=\sum_\sigma\theta(v_{\pi\sigma})=\theta(\sum_\sigma v_\sigma)$ by additivity and bijectivity of $\pi$. This is the Weil morphism condition, so $T=\operatorname{Tr}$; a Weil morphism is an underlying morphism satisfying it, so equal underlying maps are equal Weil maps. The unit is equivariant as well. The split-sheet lemma gives $T\eta=m\operatorname{id}$. Since $m\ne0$ in $\Qlb$ and $m^{-1}$ commutes with the $\Qlb$-linear $\theta$, $r=m^{-1}T$ is a Weil morphism and $r\eta=\operatorname{id}$.

proof.text: The Weil maps $\eta,r$ exhibit $\mathcal F$ as a direct summand of the mixed $P$ from Step 3. Clause (3) of mixed-direct-summand gives mixedness of $\mathcal F$ with the same bound $w$, independently of reality.

tool_uses.why: Triangularization over the algebraically closed coefficient field supplies algebraic multiplicities for powers, without assuming semisimplicity; the unit has no replacement for this linear-algebra tool.

The coefficient-compatible clopen product equivalence realizes the actual underlying inverse and direct images on geometric sheets; it is a coefficient-category tool, not a replacement of the descent route.
Its t-exactness identifies the finite derived direct image with an exact functor of the prescribed rational/common-stage hearts; its semilinear naturality identifies the sheet action.
Canonical Weil lifts of the prescribed operations and equivariance of their adjunction unit are generic functorial tools needed before the trace calculation.
Only the ordinary inverse/direct image adjunction for the finite geometric projection is used to identify the prescribed unit with the diagonal.
Only stability of finiteness under geometric base change is used to apply the finite-adic heart theorem to the geometric projection.
